title: Torsion freeness survives base change along a flat homomorphism of domains
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement is a base-change statement for torsion freeness along a flat map of domains, and the proof is a chain of three reductions that all have to be made in the correct order (statement lines 4824-4827, proof lines 4830-4837). One first sees that a torsion free M sits inside M tensor K and that flatness of R' over R keeps this injection after tensoring with R' (proof lines 4830-4833); the module M tensor K is then identified as a direct sum of copies of the fraction field so the problem is pushed to the single case K tensor R' (proof line 4834-4835), which is settled by recognising that module as a localisation of R' (proof line 4835-4836). What is not routine is the reduction step itself: it uses flatness of the ring map, not of the module, and it uses that torsion freeness is tested elementwise, so a reader cannot replace it by the (false) statement that an arbitrary tensor product of torsion free modules is torsion free.
